column3: “a public adjuration to testify” renders “the sound of an oath (alah),” and “his guilt” renders “his iniquity.”
“his guilt offering” renders “asham,” which here may mean “his penalty,” since the animal is a sin offering.
“he cannot afford” renders “his hand does not reach the sufficiency of.”
“his means are insufficient” renders “his hand does not reach,” and “incense” renders “frankincense (levonah).”
NASB adds “though” and “still” to the clauses “and he did not know and he is guilty”; “his punishment” renders “his iniquity.”
“certainly guilty” renders an emphatic doubled verb.
